knowledge:
- key_parameters: skipFactor=Factor to skip odd values in the interval [0, Inf) (default is 3), where higher values mean fewer samples are skipped ;; zeta=Threshold in the interval [0, 1] (default is 0.5) used in membership functions to control the activation of linguistic labels ;; overlapping=Integer (1, 2, or 3) determining the number of discrete labels used (1 for Low/Medium/High; 2 for 5 labels; 3 for 6 labels) ;; piVal=Threshold in the interval [0, 1] (default is 0.9) controlling the percentage of class samples required to establish a fuzzy pattern label
- alternatives: Classical gene selection/filtering methods that rank genes solely by statistical significance or discrimination metrics
- when_to_use: Appropriate for microarray or transcriptomics datasets with high dimensionality (many genes) and small sample sizes, where identifying a robust, interpretable, and reduced set of class-specific marker genes is required
- pitfalls: Running the algorithm on very large datasets (e.g., 20,000+ genes) can take several minutes; setting the piVal parameter too high may result in an overly stringent filter with very few or no genes making up the pattern; the discriminant fuzzy pattern is highly dependent on the specific set of comparison classes, meaning results will change if classes are added or removed

workflows.name: quick_discriminant_fuzzy_pattern
workflows.intent: Quickly identify differentially expressed genes from an ExpressionSet object using default parameters.
input: rmadataset (ExpressionSet object containing gene expression matrix and class labels)
workflows.stages: 1. Run the wrapper function discriminantFuzzyPattern ;; 2. Plot the resulting discriminant fuzzy patterns

workflows.name: step_by_step_fuzzy_pipeline
workflows.intent: Run the complete step-by-step fuzzy pattern discretization and discrimination pipeline starting from raw CSV files.
input: exprsData.csv (CSV file containing gene expression values)
pData.csv (CSV file containing phenotype metadata and class labels)
workflows.stages: 1. Read CSV files into an ExpressionSet ;; 2. Calculate membership functions ;; 3. Discretize expression values into linguistic labels ;; 4. Calculate fuzzy patterns for each class ;; 5. Calculate discriminant fuzzy patterns ;; 6. Plot the final discriminant fuzzy patterns
workflows.code:
library(DFP)
dataDir <- system.file("extdata", package="DFP")
fileExprs <- file.path(dataDir, "exprsData.csv")
filePhenodata <- file.path(dataDir, "pData.csv")
rmadataset <- readCSV(fileExprs, filePhenodata)
skipFactor <- 3
zeta <- 0.5
piVal <- 0.9
overlapping <- 2
mfs <- calculateMembershipFunctions(rmadataset, skipFactor)
plotMembershipFunctions(rmadataset, mfs, featureNames(rmadataset)[1:2])
dvs <- discretizeExpressionValues(rmadataset, mfs, zeta, overlapping)
showDiscreteValues(dvs, featureNames(rmadataset)[1:10],c("healthy", "AML-inv"))
fps <- calculateFuzzyPatterns(rmadataset, dvs, piVal, overlapping)
showFuzzyPatterns(fps, "healthy")[21:50]
dfps <- calculateDiscriminantFuzzyPattern(rmadataset, fps)
plotDiscriminantFuzzyPattern(dfps, overlapping)
